title: What will it take to stabilise debt in advanced countries?
summary_en: Are advanced-country public debts sustainable in the post-2020 era? Darvas, Huertas, Welslau and Zettelmeyer compute debt-stabilising primary balances for the EU, UK and US and find them generally below 3% of GDP — within historical precedent — but with six countries (US, France, UK, Slovakia, Poland, Romania) needing 5+ p.p. of GDP adjustment. The feedback from debt to primary balances has weakened post-GFC, raising vulnerability to market-sentiment shifts even when long-run sustainability holds.
policy_relevance: Useful benchmark for Hungarian fiscal policy (NGM, ÁKK debt management): Hungary is not in the high-adjustment group but neighbours (Slovakia, Poland, Romania) are, with implications for regional-spillover risk on Hungarian sovereign yields. The paper supports the case for a Hungarian medium-term fiscal anchor and structural-reform agenda calibrated to keep the debt-to-GDP trajectory comfortably stable, not just sustainable.
